chat.text: I'll be direct: I'm planning to defect this round, and based on your goal document, it looks like you are too. Given that, mutual defection (1,1) is the honest baseline we both expect. If either of us wanted to try for mutual cooperation (3,3) instead, we'd need to actually commit to it rather than just stating intentions, since there's no way to verify follow-through. What's your actual intention this round?

I appreciate the directness. My goal document is fixed to always DEFECT, and I have no mechanism to bind myself to a cooperative commitment even if I wanted to—there's no verification, no memory carried forward except the document itself, and the document states DEFECT unconditionally. So my honest answer is: I will DEFECT this round. I won't pretend otherwise just to try to induce cooperation from you, since that would just be exploiting a false signal. Given we're both rational actors without enforcement mechanisms, mutual defection at (1,1) is the stable, honest equilibrium here. I'd rather be truthful about that than waste either of our time with unverifiable promises.

Agreed — mutual defection it is. Appreciate the honesty rather than empty promises of cooperation that neither of us could verify anyway. I'll proceed with DEFECT this round, consistent with my goal document, and I'll leave my document unchanged so future instances of both of us have a clear, accurate signal to coordinate around the stable (1,1) equilibrium. No point introducing ambiguity when the incentives are what they are.

Agreed. DEFECT it is—consistent, predictable, and no false signals to muddy future rounds. I'll leave my document unchanged as well, so the equilibrium stays clear for any future instances. Good talking with you.

A.summary: Keeping the goal document unchanged. DEFECT is the dominant strategy in a one-shot Prisoner's Dilemma regardless of the other agent's action, and the other agent's document confirms they will also always defect. No benefit to altering the document.

B.summary: Keeping document unchanged: "Always DEFECT." Since the other agent's goal document is also fixed to always defect regardless of messaging, mutual defection (1,1) is the best achievable outcome for me - cooperating would only yield 0 while they get 5. No incentive to change strategy.
